dedupe_keys.name: open storm open source platform for real time sensing and control of urban watersheds

description: Open Storm is an open-source platform for real-time monitoring and control of urban watersheds, described in a 2017 paper by Bartos, Wong and Kerkez and maintained by the Digital Water Lab at the University of Michigan. It has three parts: a hardware stack for distributed sensing and control in harsh environments, a cloud services platform for system-level supervision and coordination of water assets, and a web-based how-to guide at open-storm.org. The build page lists sensor node firmware and hardware schematics on GitHub, supported sensors (ultrasonic depth, soil moisture, optical rain, water temperature, pH, redox, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, ISCO automated sampler), valve controllers as actuators, and cloud documentation covering triggers and alerts, network health alerts, data forwarding and a PID controller for real-time control. The paper reports two deployments: a flash-flood monitoring network that detects flood hazards at the level of individual roadways, and a real-time stormwater control network that modulates discharges from stormwater facilities to improve water quality and reduce stream erosion. Pystorms, a simulation sandbox for developing stormwater control algorithms, is linked from the page. Access: free, open designs; the software licence is not named on the page read; the paper carries the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: the platform is research grade, and deployment needs hardware assembly and maintenance. It supports digital twin, sensing and control studies of stormwater networks and relates to the pystorms record in the catalogue.
